questions.question: If you analyze a completely pure chemical substance using paper chromatography, what will you see on the chromatogram?
options: Only one spot
Multiple spots at different heights
A continuous streak of colors
No spots at all

questions.question: Why does a mixture of food dyes produce multiple spots at different heights on a chromatogram?
options: Because it contains only one chemical compound
Because a mixture produces many spots on a chromatogram
Because the paper has dissolved the dyes
Because the solvent has reacted with the paper

questions.question: Why is a pencil used to draw the starting line on chromatography paper instead of a pen?
options: Pencil lead is cheaper than ink
Pencil is insoluble in water
Pencil ink travels faster than the solvent
Pencil marks are magnetic

questions.question: Under what condition is simple distillation most appropriate for separating a mixture?
options: When separating a mixture containing only two substances
When separating a mixture of five different gases
When the substances have identical boiling points
When separating insoluble solids from a liquid

questions.question: When would a chemist choose fractional distillation instead of simple distillation?
options: To separate an insoluble solid from a liquid
To separate mixtures with three or more substances, or substances with similar boiling points
To attract magnetic substances from a non-magnetic mixture
To filter out large sand particles from water

questions.question: What is the consequence if the condenser warms up during a distillation experiment?
options: The condensation rate will increase
The liquid will freeze inside the condenser
The condenser becomes less effective and more gas will escape
The boiling point of the mixture will decrease

questions.question: What happens when you use evaporation to remove a solvent from a solution?
options: It leads to the production of a saturated solution
It turns the solute into a gas
It makes the remaining solution more dilute
It decreases the temperature of the solute

questions.question: Which process describes the reforming of a solute as crystals from a saturated solution following a change in conditions?
options: Filtration
Chromatography
Decanting
Crystallisation

questions.question: Where does the solvent go when a solution is left to undergo crystallisation?
options: It sinks to the bottom of the container
It evaporates into the air around you
It chemically bonds with the container
It reacts to form a new solid

questions.question: What is the effect of allowing a solvent to evaporate very slowly during crystallisation?
options: No crystals will form at all
Larger crystals form
Smaller, finer crystal powder is produced
The crystals will turn into liquid

questions.question: A student has a mixture of sand, copper, and iron filings. Which materials will be attracted if they use a magnet?
options: Only copper
Only sand
Iron and steel
Copper and iron

questions.question: How can you separate an insoluble solid, like sand, from a liquid?
options: Using a filter by a process known as filtration
By heating the mixture until it boils
By using a strong magnet
By chromatography

questions.question: What is the purpose of adding a drop of water to a filter funnel when setting up filtration?
options: To dissolve the insoluble solids beforehand
To help keep the filter paper cone open for easy filtering
To wash the funnel clean of chemical residues
To cool down the hot mixture being filtered

questions.question: What happens to immiscible liquids if they are mixed and then allowed to settle?
options: They will dissolve completely into each other
They will react chemically to form a solid
They do not mix and one will float above the other
They will instantly evaporate into the air

questions.question: Which of these methods can be used to separate two immiscible liquids?
options: Paper chromatography
Decanting or using a separating funnel
Simple distillation only
Crystallisation

questions.question: If you leave a mixture of miscible liquids in a sealed container for a long time, what will happen?
options: They will separate into distinct layers
They do not separate into layers
The bottom liquid will crystallise
They will turn into immiscible liquids

questions.question: How can the boiling points of miscible liquids be used to separate them?
options: By using a magnet to attract the lower boiling point liquid
By changing states through heating and cooling
By filtering the mixture through paper
By letting them settle into layers over time

questions.question: Which sequence of techniques is required to separate pure salt from rock salt?
options: Making a solution, filtration, and crystallisation
Simple distillation, chromatography, and magnetism
Decanting, fractional distillation, and evaporation
Filtration, chromatography, and decanting

questions.question: On what scientific principle does distillation work to separate a solution?
options: One part of a solution having a different boiling point than the other part
One component being magnetic while the other is not
The difference in particle size between solute and solvent
One substance being soluble and the other being insoluble

questions.question: Why should the condenser in a distillation setup be kept cold?
options: To prevent the glass from shattering from intense heat
To speed up condensation
To slow down the boiling rate of the mixture
To stop the solvent from evaporating in the flask
